correctness.rationale: The tie-direction count has exactly 2 per unordered pair, its tied score is independent N(0,1/2), and the conditional binomial probability yields the normalized beta identity. Direct Gaussian hull enumeration corroborates sample dimensions. Differentiating f gives f'(q)=-2 sqrt(pi) Phi^{-1}(q), strictly decreasing, and the successive first differences equal expectations over stochastically ordered Beta(k+1,n-k) laws. Symmetry, strict maxima, beta concentration, and Mills-ratio/uniform-integrability bounds establish all quantifiers and both limits. No numerical test is mistaken for infinite proof.

value.rationale: The worst-case k-set problem is mathematically motivated and its expected-rank behavior for Gaussian projections is a natural quantitative geometric question. The strict all-rank central maximizer, sharp universal upper envelope, and contrast between fixed-rank square-root-log and proportional-rank linear scaling are meaningful structural information not furnished by the general facet-count formula or bounds alone.
